source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֔ב ק֛וּם עֲלֵ֥ה בֵֽית־אֵ֖ל וְשֶׁב־שָׁ֑ם וַעֲשֵׂה־שָׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לָאֵל֙ הַנִּרְאֶ֣ה אֵלֶ֔יךָ בְּבָרְחֲךָ֔מִפְּנֵ֖י עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said God to Jacob, arise, go up [to] Bethel and dwell there, and make there an altar to the God who appeared to you when you fled from before Esau your brother.

en.L: And God said to Jacob, "Arise, go up to Bethel and dwell there, and make an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from Esau your brother."
en.B: Then God said to Jacob, "Up, and go to Bethel, and make your home there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you as you fled from your brother Esau."
en.R: God told Jacob, "Get ready and go up to Bethel. Live there, and build an altar to the God who appeared to you when you were running away from your brother Esau."

es.L: Y dijo Dios a Jacob: «Levántate, sube a Betel y habita allí, y haz allí un altar al Dios que se te apareció cuando huías de Esaú tu hermano».
es.B: Entonces Dios le dijo a Jacob: «Ponte en camino, ve a Betel y establécete allí. Construye allí un altar al Dios que se te apareció cuando huías de tu hermano Esaú».
es.R: Dios le dijo a Jacob: «Prepárate y sube a Betel. Vive allí, y construye un altar al Dios que se te apareció cuando escapabas de tu hermano Esaú».

fr.L: Et Dieu dit à Jacob : « Lève-toi, monte à Béthel et habites-y, et fais là un autel au Dieu qui t’est apparu quand tu fuyais devant Ésaü ton frère. »
fr.B: Puis Dieu dit à Jacob : « Debout ! Va à Béthel et installe-toi là-bas. Bâtis-y un autel au Dieu qui t’est apparu lorsque tu fuyais ton frère Ésaü. »
fr.R: Dieu a dit à Jacob : « Prépare-toi et monte à Béthel. Habite là-bas, et construis un autel au Dieu qui t’est apparu quand tu t’enfuyais loin de ton frère Ésaü. »

sw.L: Mungu alimwambia Yakobo, "Inuka, panda kwenda Betheli ukae huko, na ufanye huko madhabahu kwa Mungu aliyekutokea ulipomkimbia Esau ndugu yako."
sw.B: Kisha Mungu akamwambia Yakobo, "Ondoka, uende Betheli ukaishi huko. Mjengee huko madhabahu Mungu aliyekutokea ulipokuwa ukimkimbia ndugu yako Esau."
sw.R: Mungu alimwambia Yakobo, "Jiandae, upande kwenda Betheli. Kaa huko, ujenge madhabahu kwa ajili ya Mungu aliyekutokea ulipokuwa ukimkimbia ndugu yako Esau."

decisions.choice: Bethel, the God who appeared to you: the vow comes due
decisions.reason: At Bethel Jacob saw the stairway and vowed that if God brought him back safely, the LORD would be his God and the stone would become God's house (28:10-22). God now calls him back to keep that vow.

decisions.choice: go up: Bethel lies higher than Shechem
decisions.reason: Bethel is in the hill country, higher than Shechem. "Going up" is also the usual phrase for going to a place of worship.

decisions.choice: the God who appeared to you: God speaks of himself in the third person
decisions.reason: God refers to himself as "the God (El) who appeared to you", pointing Jacob back to the earlier meeting rather than simply saying "me".

decisions.choice: passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R)
decisions.reason: The narrative tense follows the French style guide: the passé simple ("dit"), the normal tense of written narrative, at Literal and Balanced; the passé composé ("a dit"), as French is spoken and read in school today, at Readable. Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־בֵּית֔וֹ וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ הָסִ֜רוּ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַנֵּכָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתֹכְכֶ֔ם וְהִֽטַּהֲר֔וּ וְהַחֲלִ֖יפוּ שִׂמְלֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jacob to his household and to all who [were] with him, remove the gods of foreignness which [are] among you, and purify yourselves and change your clothes.

en.L: And Jacob said to his household and to all who [were] with him, "Put away the foreign gods that [are] among you, and purify yourselves and change your clothes.
en.B: So Jacob told his family and everyone with him, "Get rid of every foreign god you have among you. Make yourselves clean and put on fresh clothes.
en.R: So Jacob spoke to his family and to everyone traveling with him. "Throw away all the statues of other gods that you have," he said. "Wash yourselves and put on clean clothes.

es.L: Y dijo Jacob a su casa y a todos los que [estaban] con él: «{{plural_you:Quiten|Quitad}} los dioses extraños que [hay] entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:purifíquense|purificaos}} y {{plural_you:cambien|cambiad}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} vestidos.
es.B: Así que Jacob dijo a su familia y a todos los que lo acompañaban: «{{plural_you:Desháganse|Deshaceos}} de todos los dioses extranjeros que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Purifíquense|Purificaos}} y {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} ropa limpia.
es.R: Entonces Jacob habló con su familia y con todos los que viajaban con él. «{{plural_you:Tiren|Tirad}} todas las estatuas de otros dioses que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} —les dijo—. {{plural_you:Lávense|Lavaos}} y {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} ropa limpia.

fr.L: Et Jacob dit à sa maison et à tous ceux qui [étaient] avec lui : « Ôtez les dieux étrangers qui [sont] au milieu de vous, purifiez-vous et changez de vêtements.
fr.B: Jacob dit donc à sa famille et à tous ceux qui l’accompagnaient : « Débarrassez-vous de tous les dieux étrangers que vous avez parmi vous. Purifiez-vous et mettez des vêtements propres.
fr.R: Alors Jacob a parlé à sa famille et à tous ceux qui voyageaient avec lui. « Jetez toutes les statues d’autres dieux que vous avez, a-t-il dit. Lavez-vous et mettez des vêtements propres.

sw.L: Naye Yakobo akawaambia watu wa nyumba yake na wote [waliokuwa] pamoja naye, "Ondoeni miungu ya kigeni iliyo kati yenu, mjitakase, mbadilishe nguo zenu.
sw.B: Basi Yakobo akawaambia jamaa yake na wote waliokuwa pamoja naye, "Tupilieni mbali kila mungu wa kigeni mlio naye kati yenu. Jitakaseni, mvae nguo safi.
sw.R: Basi Yakobo akazungumza na jamaa yake na wote waliosafiri pamoja naye. Akasema, "Tupeni sanamu zote za miungu mingine mlizo nazo. Jiosheni, mvae nguo safi.

decisions.choice: the foreign gods among you: idols carried by the household
decisions.reason: The household included Rachel, who had taken her father's household gods (31:19, 34), and probably the captives taken at Shechem (34:29). Before meeting God at Bethel the family must belong to him alone, as Joshua later demanded of Israel at Shechem (Joshua 24:14, 23).

decisions.choice: purify yourselves and change your clothes: making ready to meet God
decisions.reason: Washing and changing clothes prepared people to come before God; Israel did so before Sinai (Exodus 19:10, 14).

decisions.choice: statues of other gods
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gods were: images that could be handed over and buried (verse 4).

source.text: וְנָק֥וּמָה וְנַעֲלֶ֖ה בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־שָּׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֗חַ לָאֵ֞ל הָעֹנֶ֤ה אֹתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם צָֽרָתִ֔י וַיְהִי֙ עִמָּדִ֔י בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽכְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And let us arise and let us go up [to] Bethel, and I will make there an altar to the God who answered me in [the] day of my distress, and he has been with me on the way which I have gone.

en.L: And let us arise and go up to Bethel, and I will make an altar there to the God who answered me in the day of my distress and has been with me on the way I have gone."
en.B: Then let us set out and go up to Bethel. I will make an altar there to the God who answered me when I was in trouble and has stayed with me on every road I have traveled."
en.R: Then let us go up to Bethel. There I will build an altar to the God who answered me when I was in great trouble. God has been with me everywhere I have gone."

es.L: Y levantémonos y subamos a Betel, y haré allí un altar al Dios que me respondió en el día de mi angustia y ha estado conmigo en el camino que he andado».
es.B: Luego pongámonos en marcha y subamos a Betel. Allí haré un altar al Dios que me respondió cuando estaba en apuros y que me ha acompañado en todos los caminos que he recorrido».
es.R: Después subamos a Betel. Allí construiré un altar al Dios que me respondió cuando yo estaba en un gran aprieto. Dios ha estado conmigo en todas partes adonde he ido».

fr.L: Et levons-nous, montons à Béthel, et je ferai là un autel au Dieu qui m’a répondu au jour de ma détresse et qui a été avec moi sur le chemin où j’ai marché. »
fr.B: Puis mettons-nous en route et montons à Béthel. J’y ferai un autel au Dieu qui m’a répondu quand j’étais dans la détresse et qui m’a accompagné sur toutes les routes que j’ai parcourues. »
fr.R: Ensuite, montons à Béthel. Là, je construirai un autel au Dieu qui m’a répondu quand j’avais de gros problèmes. Dieu a été avec moi partout où je suis allé. »

sw.L: Na tuinuke, tupande kwenda Betheli, nami nitafanya huko madhabahu kwa Mungu aliyenijibu siku ya taabu yangu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} amekuwa pamoja nami katika njia niliyoiendea."
sw.B: Kisha tuondoke, tupande Betheli. Huko nitamfanyia madhabahu Mungu aliyenijibu nilipokuwa katika dhiki, aliyekaa pamoja nami kila njia niliyopita."
sw.R: Kisha tupande kwenda Betheli. Huko nitajenga madhabahu kwa ajili ya Mungu aliyenijibu nilipokuwa katika taabu kubwa. Mungu amekuwa pamoja nami kila mahali nilipokwenda."

decisions.choice: the day of my distress: Jacob's flight from Esau
decisions.reason: Jacob fled with nothing but his staff (32:11), and in fear of Esau prayed for rescue (32:12). God had promised at Bethel, "I am with you and will keep you wherever you go" (28:15); Jacob now says that God kept it.

source.text: וַיִּתְּנ֣וּ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֗ב אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַנֵּכָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָדָ֔ם וְאֶת־הַנְּזָמִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאָזְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּטְמֹ֤ן אֹתָם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב תַּ֥חַת הָאֵלָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִם־שְׁכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they gave to Jacob all the gods of foreignness which [were] in their hand and the rings which [were] in their ears, and hid them Jacob under the terebinth which [was] near Shechem.

en.L: And they gave Jacob all the foreign gods that [were] in their hands and the rings that [were] in their ears, and Jacob hid them under the terebinth that [was] near Shechem.
en.B: They handed over to Jacob all the foreign gods they had, along with the rings from their ears, and Jacob buried them under the great tree near Shechem.
en.R: So they gave Jacob all the statues of other gods. They also gave him the rings they wore in their ears. Jacob buried all of them under the big oak tree near Shechem.

es.L: Y dieron a Jacob todos los dioses extraños que [estaban] en sus manos y los anillos que [estaban] en sus orejas, y Jacob los escondió debajo de la encina que [está] junto a Siquem.
es.B: Ellos entregaron a Jacob todos los dioses extranjeros que tenían, junto con los anillos de sus orejas, y Jacob los enterró debajo del gran árbol que está cerca de Siquem.
es.R: Así que le dieron a Jacob todas las estatuas de otros dioses. También le dieron los aretes que llevaban en las orejas. Jacob lo enterró todo debajo de la gran encina que había cerca de Siquem.

fr.L: Et ils donnèrent à Jacob tous les dieux étrangers qui [étaient] dans leurs mains et les anneaux qui [étaient] à leurs oreilles, et Jacob les cacha sous le térébinthe qui [est] près de Sichem.
fr.B: Ils remirent à Jacob tous les dieux étrangers qu’ils avaient, ainsi que les anneaux de leurs oreilles, et Jacob les enfouit sous le grand arbre qui est près de Sichem.
fr.R: Alors ils ont donné à Jacob toutes les statues d’autres dieux. Ils lui ont aussi donné les boucles qu’ils portaient aux oreilles. Jacob a tout enterré sous le grand chêne, près de Sichem.

sw.L: Nao wakampa Yakobo miungu yote ya kigeni [iliyokuwa] mikononi mwao na pete [zilizokuwa] masikioni mwao, naye Yakobo akavificha chini ya mti mkubwa [ulioko] karibu na Shekemu.
sw.B: Wakamkabidhi Yakobo miungu yote ya kigeni waliyokuwa nayo, pamoja na pete za masikioni mwao, naye Yakobo akavifukia chini ya mti mkubwa ulio karibu na Shekemu.
sw.R: Basi wakampa Yakobo sanamu zote za miungu mingine. Wakampa pia pete walizovaa masikioni. Yakobo akavifukia vyote chini ya mwaloni mkubwa karibu na Shekemu.

decisions.choice: the rings in their ears: jewelry linked with the worship of other gods
decisions.reason: Earrings could serve as amulets or bear the marks of gods. Gold earrings were later melted down to make the golden calf (Exodus 32:2-4).

decisions.choice: the terebinth: a great tree, a landmark at Shechem
decisions.reason: The 'elah is a large, long-lived tree, the terebinth or an oak. Abraham camped by the great tree of Moreh at Shechem (12:6), and Joshua later set up a stone under the oak there (Joshua 24:26).

decisions.choice: buried
decisions.reason: The verb taman means to hide by burying (Joshua 7:21). Balanced and Readable say "buried"; Literal keeps "hid".

source.text: וַיִּסָּ֑עוּ וַיְהִ֣י׀חִתַּ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֗ים עַל־הֶֽעָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ סְבִיבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם וְלֹ֣א רָֽדְפ֔וּ אַחֲרֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out, and there was [the] terror of God on the cities which [were] around them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.

en.L: And they set out, and a terror from God was on the cities around them, and they did not pursue the sons of Jacob.
en.B: As they moved on, a dread sent by God came over the towns around them, and no one went after Jacob's sons.
en.R: Then they left. God made the people in all the nearby towns very afraid, so no one chased after Jacob's sons.

es.L: Y partieron, y hubo terror de Dios sobre las ciudades que [estaban] alrededor de ellos, y no persiguieron a los hijos de Jacob.
es.B: Mientras avanzaban, un pavor enviado por Dios cayó sobre los pueblos de alrededor, y nadie fue tras los hijos de Jacob.
es.R: Luego se fueron. Dios hizo que la gente de todos los pueblos cercanos tuviera mucho miedo, y por eso nadie persiguió a los hijos de Jacob.

fr.L: Et ils partirent, et une terreur de Dieu fut sur les villes qui [étaient] autour d’eux, et ils ne poursuivirent pas les fils de Jacob.
fr.B: Pendant qu’ils avançaient, une épouvante envoyée par Dieu saisit les villes des alentours, et personne ne se lança à la poursuite des fils de Jacob.
fr.R: Puis ils sont partis. Dieu a fait très peur aux gens de toutes les villes voisines, et personne n’a poursuivi les fils de Jacob.

sw.L: Wakasafiri, na hofu ya Mungu ikawa juu ya miji [iliyokuwa] kandokando yao, wala hawakuwafuatia wana wa Yakobo.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakiendelea na safari, hofu kuu iliyotoka kwa Mungu ikaiangukia miji iliyowazunguka, wala hakuna aliyewafuatia wana wa Yakobo.
sw.R: Kisha wakaondoka. Mungu akawatia hofu kuu watu wa miji yote ya jirani, kwa hiyo hakuna aliyewafukuza wana wa Yakobo.

decisions.choice: terror of God: a fear God sent on the people
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean a fear that God sent, or simply a very great fear. Jacob had feared the peoples of the land would attack (34:30); God protects the family in spite of what Simeon and Levi had done. The same holy fear goes before Israel in Exodus 23:27.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב ל֗וּזָה אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן הִ֖וא בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל ה֖וּא וְכָל־הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Jacob to Luz, which [is] in [the] land of Canaan, that [is] Bethel, he and all the people who [were] with him.

en.L: And Jacob came to Luz, which [is] in the land of Canaan, that [is], Bethel, he and all the people who [were] with him.
en.B: Jacob arrived at Luz in the land of Canaan, the place now known as Bethel, together with all the people in his company.
en.R: Jacob and all his people came to Luz in the land of Canaan. Luz is also called Bethel.

es.L: Y llegó Jacob a Luz, que [está] en la tierra de Canaán, esto [es], Betel, él y todo el pueblo que [estaba] con él.
es.B: Jacob llegó a Luz, en la tierra de Canaán, el lugar que ahora se conoce como Betel, junto con toda la gente que lo acompañaba.
es.R: Jacob y toda su gente llegaron a Luz, en la tierra de Canaán. A Luz también se la llama Betel.

fr.L: Et Jacob arriva à Louz, qui [est] dans le pays de Canaan, c’est-à-dire Béthel, lui et tout le peuple qui [était] avec lui.
fr.B: Jacob arriva à Louz, dans le pays de Canaan, le lieu qu’on appelle aujourd’hui Béthel, avec tous les gens de sa troupe.
fr.R: Jacob et tous ses gens sont arrivés à Louz, dans le pays de Canaan. Louz s’appelle aussi Béthel.

sw.L: Naye Yakobo akafika Luzu, [ulioko] katika nchi ya Kanaani, yaani, Betheli, yeye na watu wote [waliokuwa] pamoja naye.
sw.B: Yakobo akafika Luzu katika nchi ya Kanaani, mahali panapojulikana sasa kama Betheli, pamoja na watu wote aliokuwa nao.
sw.R: Yakobo na watu wake wote wakafika Luzu katika nchi ya Kanaani. Luzu unaitwa pia Betheli.

decisions.choice: Luz, that is, Bethel: the town's old name and its new one
decisions.reason: The town was called Luz; Jacob named the place Bethel, "house of God", after his dream there (28:19).

source.text: וַיִּ֤בֶן שָׁם֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ וַיִּקְרָא֙ לַמָּק֔וֹם אֵ֖ל בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל כִּ֣י שָׁ֗ם נִגְל֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּבָרְח֖וֹ מִפְּנֵ֥י אָחִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he built there an altar and called the place El-Bethel, for there had revealed themselves to him God when he fled from before his brother.

en.L: And he built an altar there and called the place El-Bethel, because there God had revealed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to him when he fled from his brother.
en.B: There he built an altar and named the place El-Bethel, "God of Bethel", because it was there God had shown {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to him as he was fleeing from his brother.
en.R: Jacob built an altar there. He called the place El-Bethel, which means "the God of Bethel." He chose this name because God had shown {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to Jacob there when he was running away from his brother.

es.L: Y edificó allí un altar y llamó al lugar El-Betel, porque allí se le había revelado Dios cuando huía de su hermano.
es.B: Allí construyó un altar y llamó al lugar El-Betel, «Dios de Betel», porque fue allí donde Dios se le había manifestado cuando huía de su hermano.
es.R: Jacob construyó allí un altar. Llamó al lugar El-Betel, que quiere decir «el Dios de Betel». Eligió ese nombre porque Dios se le había mostrado allí a Jacob cuando escapaba de su hermano.

fr.L: Et il bâtit là un autel et appela le lieu El-Béthel, car c’est là que Dieu s’était révélé à lui quand il fuyait devant son frère.
fr.B: Il y bâtit un autel et nomma le lieu El-Béthel, « Dieu de Béthel », car c’est là que Dieu s’était montré à lui lorsqu’il fuyait son frère.
fr.R: Jacob a construit un autel à cet endroit. Il l’a appelé El-Béthel, ce qui veut dire « le Dieu de Béthel ». Il a choisi ce nom parce que c’est là que Dieu s’était montré à Jacob quand il s’enfuyait loin de son frère.

sw.L: Akajenga huko madhabahu, akapaita mahali pale El-betheli, kwa sababu huko Mungu alikuwa amejifunua kwake alipokuwa akimkimbia ndugu yake.
sw.B: Huko akajenga madhabahu, akapaita mahali pale El-betheli, yaani "Mungu wa Betheli", kwa kuwa ni huko Mungu alikomtokea alipokuwa akimkimbia ndugu yake.
sw.R: Yakobo akajenga madhabahu huko. Akapaita mahali pale El-betheli, maana yake "Mungu wa Betheli." Alichagua jina hilo kwa sababu Mungu alikuwa amejionyesha kwake huko alipokuwa akimkimbia ndugu yake.

decisions.choice: El-Bethel: the God of Bethel
decisions.reason: Jacob names the place after the God he met there, not only the place itself (31:13, "I am the God of Bethel").

decisions.choice: God had revealed himself: the verb is plural
alternatives: the divine beings had revealed themselves
decisions.reason: Elohim, "God", is plural in form, and here the verb is plural too, as sometimes happens (20:13). The sense is God, the one who appeared; the plural may also recall the angels Jacob saw going up and down (28:12).

decisions.choice: God had revealed himself
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, but its subject is the one God (m2), so every level uses the singular "himself".

source.text: וַתָּ֤מָת דְּבֹרָה֙ מֵינֶ֣קֶת רִבְקָ֔ה וַתִּקָּבֵ֛ר מִתַּ֥חַת לְבֵֽית־אֵ֖ל תַּ֣חַת הָֽאַלּ֑וֹן וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ אַלּ֥וֹן בָּכֽוּת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And died Deborah, [the] nurse of Rebekah, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and he called its name Allon-bacuth.

en.L: And Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and its name was called Allon-bacuth.
en.B: Deborah, who had nursed Rebekah, died there and was buried beneath the oak below Bethel. So the tree came to be called Allon-bacuth, "Oak of Weeping".
en.R: Rebekah's old nurse Deborah died. They buried her under the oak tree below Bethel. So that tree was named Allon-bacuth, which means "Oak of Weeping."

es.L: Y murió Débora, nodriza de Rebeca, y fue sepultada debajo de Betel, bajo la encina; y se le dio el nombre de Alón-bacut.
es.B: Débora, la que había criado a Rebeca, murió allí y fue sepultada bajo la encina que está más abajo de Betel. Por eso aquel árbol recibió el nombre de Alón-bacut, «Encina del Llanto».
es.R: Débora, la anciana nodriza de Rebeca, murió. La enterraron bajo la encina que está más abajo de Betel. Por eso aquel árbol se llamó Alón-bacut, que quiere decir «Encina del Llanto».

fr.L: Et Débora, la nourrice de Rébecca, mourut, et elle fut enterrée au-dessous de Béthel, sous le chêne ; et on lui donna le nom d’Allôn-Bakouth.
fr.B: Débora, qui avait été la nourrice de Rébecca, mourut là et fut enterrée sous le chêne, en contrebas de Béthel. Aussi appela-t-on cet arbre Allôn-Bakouth, « Chêne des Pleurs ».
fr.R: Débora, la vieille nourrice de Rébecca, est morte. On l’a enterrée sous le chêne, en dessous de Béthel. C’est pourquoi on a appelé cet arbre Allôn-Bakouth, ce qui veut dire « Chêne des Pleurs ».

sw.L: Naye Debora, mlezi wa Rebeka, akafa, akazikwa chini ya Betheli chini ya mwaloni; nao ukaitwa jina lake Aloni-bakuthi.
sw.B: Debora, aliyekuwa mlezi wa Rebeka, akafa huko, akazikwa chini ya mwaloni ulio chini ya Betheli. Kwa hiyo mti huo ukaitwa Aloni-bakuthi, yaani "Mwaloni wa Kilio".
sw.R: Debora, mlezi wa zamani wa Rebeka, akafa. Wakamzika chini ya mwaloni ulio chini ya Betheli. Kwa hiyo mti huo ukaitwa Aloni-bakuthi, maana yake "Mwaloni wa Kilio."

decisions.choice: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse: a lifelong servant of the family
decisions.reason: A nurse went with Rebekah when she left home to marry Isaac (24:59); only here is she named. Her death is mourned as a loss to the whole family. Rebekah's own death is never told.

decisions.choice: Allon-bacuth: oak of weeping
decisions.reason: Allon means oak and bakhut weeping. The name keeps the memory of the mourning for her.

decisions.choice: its name was called
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject: someone, or people in general, gave the name. Literal and Balanced use the passive.

source.text: וַיֵּרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹב֙ ע֔וֹד בְּבֹא֖וֹ מִפַּדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֑ם וַיְבָ֖רֶךְ אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And appeared God to Jacob again when he came from Paddan-aram, and he blessed him.

en.L: And God appeared to Jacob again when he came from Paddan-aram, and blessed him.
en.B: Now that Jacob had come back from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him once more and blessed him.
en.R: God appeared to Jacob a second time, now that he was back from Paddan-aram, and God blessed him.

es.L: Y se apareció Dios a Jacob otra vez, cuando venía de Padán Aram, y lo bendijo.
es.B: Ahora que Jacob había vuelto de Padán Aram, Dios se le apareció una vez más y lo bendijo.
es.R: Dios se le apareció a Jacob por segunda vez, ahora que había vuelto de Padán Aram, y Dios lo bendijo.

fr.L: Et Dieu apparut encore à Jacob, quand il revenait de Paddân-Aram, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le bénit.
fr.B: Maintenant que Jacob était revenu de Paddân-Aram, Dieu lui apparut une fois de plus et le bénit.
fr.R: Dieu est apparu à Jacob une deuxième fois, maintenant qu’il était revenu de Paddân-Aram, et Dieu l’a béni.

sw.L: Mungu akamtokea Yakobo tena, alipokuja kutoka Padan-aramu, akambariki.
sw.B: Yakobo alipokuwa amerudi kutoka Padan-aramu, Mungu akamtokea mara nyingine tena, akambariki.
sw.R: Mungu akamtokea Yakobo mara ya pili, sasa alipokuwa amerudi kutoka Padan-aramu, naye Mungu akambariki.

decisions.choice: again: a second appearance at Bethel
decisions.reason: God first appeared to Jacob here as he left the land (28:13-15). Now he appears again on Jacob's return, closing the circle of the journey.

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ל֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים שִׁמְךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֑ב לֹֽא־יִקָּרֵא֩ שִׁמְךָ֨ע֜וֹד יַעֲקֹ֗ב כִּ֤י אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him God, your name [is] Jacob; not will be called your name again Jacob, but Israel will be your name. And he called his name Israel.

en.L: And God said to him, "Your name [is] Jacob; your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel will be your name." And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called his name Israel.
en.B: God said to him, "Your name is Jacob, but from now on that will not be your name. Your name will be Israel." So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him the name Israel.
en.R: God said to him, "Your name is Jacob. But people will not call you Jacob anymore. From now on your name is Israel." So God named him Israel.

es.L: Y le dijo Dios: «Tu nombre [es] Jacob; no se llamará más tu nombre Jacob, sino que Israel será tu nombre». Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le dio por nombre Israel.
es.B: Dios le dijo: «Te llamas Jacob, pero desde ahora ya no será ese tu nombre. Tu nombre será Israel». Así que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le dio el nombre de Israel.
es.R: Dios le dijo: «Te llamas Jacob. Pero la gente ya no te llamará Jacob. Desde ahora tu nombre es Israel». Así que Dios le puso por nombre Israel.

fr.L: Et Dieu lui dit : « Ton nom [est] Jacob ; ton nom ne sera plus appelé Jacob, mais Israël sera ton nom. » Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’appela du nom d’Israël.
fr.B: Dieu lui dit : « Tu t’appelles Jacob, mais désormais ce ne sera plus ton nom. Ton nom sera Israël. » Ainsi {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui donna le nom d’Israël.
fr.R: Dieu lui a dit : « Tu t’appelles Jacob. Mais on ne t’appellera plus Jacob. À partir de maintenant, ton nom est Israël. » Ainsi, Dieu l’a appelé Israël.

sw.L: Mungu akamwambia, "Jina lako [ni] Yakobo; jina lako halitaitwa tena Yakobo, bali Israeli litakuwa jina lako." Akamwita jina lake Israeli.
sw.B: Mungu akamwambia, "Jina lako ni Yakobo, lakini tangu sasa hilo halitakuwa jina lako. Jina lako litakuwa Israeli." Basi akampa jina Israeli.
sw.R: Mungu akamwambia, "Jina lako ni Yakobo. Lakini watu hawatakuita Yakobo tena. Tangu sasa jina lako ni Israeli." Basi Mungu akamwita Israeli.

decisions.choice: Israel will be your name: the name given at the Jabbok confirmed
decisions.reason: The man who wrestled with Jacob gave him this name (32:29). God now confirms it at Bethel, as God renamed Abram and Sarai when making the covenant (17:5, 15). Israel probably means "God strives" or "he strives with God".

decisions.choice: God (for "he")
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who gave the name; Literal and Balanced keep the pronoun.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le dio por nombre
alternatives: le dio por nombre, with no span
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject inside the verb, which would leave the English deity pronoun span with nothing to sit on. Here the explicit "él" also marks the change of subject back to God after his words to Jacob, so Literal and Balanced write it and give it the span.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֲנִ֨י אֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ פְּרֵ֣ה וּרְבֵ֔ה גּ֛וֹי וּקְהַ֥ל גּוֹיִ֖ם יִהְיֶ֣ה מִמֶּ֑ךָּ וּמְלָכִ֖ים מֵחֲלָצֶ֥יךָ יֵצֵֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him God, I [am] God Almighty; be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations will be from you, and kings from your loins will come out.

en.L: And God said to him, "I [am] God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply. A nation and an assembly of nations will come from you, and kings will come out of your body.
en.B: God also said to him, "I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and grow in number. A nation, a whole assembly of nations, will come from you, and kings will be born from your line.
en.R: God also said to him, "I am God Almighty. Have many children, and let your family grow. Your family will become a nation, and many nations. Kings will come from your family.

es.L: Y le dijo Dios: «Yo [soy] el Dios Todopoderoso: fructifica y multiplícate. Una nación y una asamblea de naciones saldrán de ti, y reyes saldrán de tu cuerpo.
es.B: Dios también le dijo: «Yo soy el Dios Todopoderoso. Sé fecundo y multiplícate. De ti saldrá una nación, toda una asamblea de naciones, y de tu linaje nacerán reyes.
es.R: Dios también le dijo: «Yo soy el Dios Todopoderoso. Ten muchos hijos, y que tu familia crezca. Tu familia llegará a ser una nación, y muchas naciones. De tu familia saldrán reyes.

fr.L: Et Dieu lui dit : « Je [suis] le Dieu tout-puissant : sois fécond et multiplie. Une nation et une assemblée de nations viendront de toi, et des rois sortiront de ton corps.
fr.B: Dieu lui dit encore : « Je suis le Dieu tout-puissant. Sois fécond et deviens nombreux. Une nation, toute une assemblée de nations, viendra de toi, et des rois naîtront de ta descendance.
fr.R: Dieu lui a dit aussi : « Je suis le Dieu tout-puissant. Aie beaucoup d’enfants, et que ta famille s’agrandisse. Ta famille deviendra une nation, et même beaucoup de nations. Des rois viendront de ta famille.

sw.L: Mungu akamwambia, "Mimi [ni] Mungu Mwenyezi; zaa ukaongezeke. Taifa na kusanyiko la mataifa litatoka kwako, na wafalme watatoka katika mwili wako.
sw.B: Mungu akamwambia pia, "Mimi ni Mungu Mwenyezi. Zaa, uongezeke. Taifa, naam, kusanyiko zima la mataifa, litatoka kwako, na wafalme watazaliwa katika uzao wako.
sw.R: Mungu akamwambia pia, "Mimi ni Mungu Mwenyezi. Zaa watoto wengi, na jamaa yako iongezeke. Jamaa yako itakuwa taifa, naam, mataifa mengi. Wafalme watatoka katika jamaa yako.

decisions.choice: God Almighty: El Shaddai
decisions.reason: The name with which God made the covenant with Abraham (17:1) and with which Isaac blessed Jacob (28:3). Its exact meaning is uncertain; the ancient translations took it as "the Almighty".

decisions.choice: be fruitful and multiply ... kings: the blessing of creation and of Abraham
decisions.reason: The command of 1:28 and 9:1 and the promise of nations and kings to Abraham (17:6) are now given to Jacob. Isaac had prayed for the same "assembly of peoples" (28:3).

decisions.choice: from your loins: from your own body, your descendants
decisions.reason: The loins are the seat of a man's power to father children.

source.text: וְאֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛תִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם וּלְיִצְחָ֖ק לְךָ֣ אֶתְּנֶ֑נָּה וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֥ אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ אֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the land which I gave to Abraham and to Isaac, to you I will give it, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.

en.L: And the land that I gave to Abraham and to Isaac I will give to you, and to your offspring after you I will give the land."
en.B: The land that I gave to Abraham and to Isaac is yours; I give it to you, and to your descendants after you I will give the land."
en.R: I gave this land to Abraham and Isaac. Now I will give it to you and to your descendants after you."

es.L: Y la tierra que di a Abraham y a Isaac, a ti te la daré, y a tu descendencia después de ti daré la tierra».
es.B: La tierra que di a Abraham y a Isaac es tuya; te la doy a ti, y a tus descendientes después de ti les daré la tierra».
es.R: Yo les di esta tierra a Abraham y a Isaac. Ahora te la daré a ti y a tus descendientes después de ti».

fr.L: Et le pays que j’ai donné à Abraham et à Isaac, je te le donnerai, et à ta descendance après toi je donnerai le pays. »
fr.B: Le pays que j’ai donné à Abraham et à Isaac est à toi ; je te le donne, et à ta descendance après toi je donnerai ce pays. »
fr.R: J’ai donné ce pays à Abraham et à Isaac. Maintenant, je vais te le donner, à toi et à tes descendants après toi. »

sw.L: Na nchi niliyowapa Abrahamu na Isaka, nitakupa wewe, na uzao wako baada yako nitawapa nchi hii."
sw.B: Nchi niliyowapa Abrahamu na Isaka ni yako; nakupa wewe, na uzao wako baada yako nitawapa nchi hii."
sw.R: Niliwapa Abrahamu na Isaka nchi hii. Sasa nitakupa wewe na wazao wako baada yako."

decisions.choice: I will give the land: the promise passed to the third generation
decisions.reason: The gift of the land runs through the promises to Abraham (12:7; 13:15; 17:8) and Isaac (26:3). Jacob now receives it in full, back in the land after his years away.

source.text: וַיַּ֥עַל מֵעָלָ֖יו אֱלֹהִ֑ים בַּמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up from him God at the place where he had spoken with him.

en.L: And God went up from him at the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken with him.
en.B: And God rose and left him there, at the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been speaking with him.
en.R: Then God left Jacob and went up from the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had talked with him.

es.L: Y subió Dios de junto a él, en el lugar donde había hablado con él.
es.B: Y Dios se elevó y lo dejó allí, en el lugar donde había estado hablando con él.
es.R: Luego Dios dejó a Jacob y subió desde el lugar donde había hablado con él.

fr.L: Et Dieu monta d’auprès de lui, au lieu où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait parlé avec lui.
fr.B: Puis Dieu s’éleva et le quitta, à l’endroit même où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’était entretenu avec lui.
fr.R: Ensuite, Dieu a quitté Jacob et s’est élevé de l’endroit où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui avait parlé.

sw.L: Mungu akapanda juu kutoka kwake, mahali pale aliposema naye.
sw.B: Kisha Mungu akapaa, akamwacha pale mahali alipokuwa akizungumza naye.
sw.R: Kisha Mungu akamwacha Yakobo, akapanda juu kutoka mahali alipozungumza naye.

decisions.choice: God went up from him: the end of the appearance
decisions.reason: The same words close God's appearance to Abraham in 17:22.

source.text: וַיַּצֵּ֨ב יַעֲקֹ֜ב מַצֵּבָ֗ה בַּמָּק֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ מַצֶּ֣בֶת אָ֑בֶן וַיַּסֵּ֤ךְ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ נֶ֔סֶךְ וַיִּצֹ֥ק עָלֶ֖יהָ שָֽׁמֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: And set up Jacob a pillar at the place where he had spoken with him, a pillar of stone, and he poured on it a drink offering and poured on it oil.

en.L: And Jacob set up a pillar at the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken with him, a pillar of stone, and he poured a drink offering on it and poured oil on it.
en.B: There, where God had spoken with him, Jacob raised a standing stone, and he poured a drink offering over it and oil as well.
en.R: Jacob set up a large stone as a marker in the place where God had talked to him. He poured wine on it as an offering, and he poured olive oil on it too.

es.L: Y Jacob erigió un pilar en el lugar donde había hablado con él, un pilar de piedra, y derramó sobre él una libación y derramó sobre él aceite.
es.B: Allí, donde Dios había hablado con él, Jacob levantó una estela de piedra, y derramó sobre ella una libación y también aceite.
es.R: Jacob colocó una piedra grande como señal en el lugar donde Dios había hablado con él. Derramó vino sobre ella como ofrenda, y también le echó aceite de oliva.

fr.L: Et Jacob dressa une stèle au lieu où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait parlé avec lui, une stèle de pierre, et il versa sur elle une libation et répandit sur elle de l’huile.
fr.B: Là où Dieu avait parlé avec lui, Jacob dressa une pierre levée ; il y versa une libation, et aussi de l’huile.
fr.R: Jacob a mis une grande pierre comme repère à l’endroit où Dieu lui avait parlé. Il a versé du vin dessus en offrande, et il y a aussi versé de l’huile d’olive.

sw.L: Naye Yakobo akasimamisha nguzo mahali pale aliposema naye, nguzo ya jiwe, akamimina juu yake sadaka ya kinywaji, akamimina juu yake mafuta.
sw.B: Pale Mungu aliposema naye, Yakobo akasimamisha jiwe la ukumbusho, akamimina juu yake sadaka ya kinywaji, na mafuta pia.
sw.R: Yakobo akasimamisha jiwe kubwa kama alama mahali pale Mungu alipozungumza naye. Akamimina divai juu yake kama sadaka, akamimina pia mafuta ya zeituni juu yake.

decisions.choice: a pillar: a standing stone marking a holy place
decisions.reason: Jacob had set up and anointed a stone at Bethel before (28:18). Standing stones marked places where something important had happened; later, pillars at the shrines of other gods were forbidden (Deuteronomy 16:22).

decisions.choice: a drink offering: wine poured out to God
decisions.reason: This is the first drink offering in Scripture. In later worship, wine was poured out alongside the sacrifices (Numbers 15:5-10).

decisions.choice: God (for "he")
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God to make clear who spoke. Literal keeps the pronoun, with the deity pronoun span.

decisions.choice: un pilar (L); una estela (B)
decisions.reason: The matsevah is a standing stone (m1). "Pilar" keeps the plain word at Literal; Balanced says "estela", the word for an upright stone set up as a marker, where the English Balanced says "standing stone". "Columna" would suggest a building. The same words are used in verse 20.

decisions.choice: une stèle (L); une pierre levée (B)
decisions.reason: The matsevah is a standing stone (m1). French "stèle" names an upright stone set up as a marker; Balanced says "pierre levée", the everyday term, where the English Balanced says "standing stone". "Colonne" would suggest a building. The same words are used in verse 20.

decisions.choice: nguzo (L); jiwe la ukumbusho (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "nguzo", the plain word for an upright post or pillar; Balanced says "jiwe la ukumbusho", a memorial stone, where the English Balanced says "standing stone". The same words are used in verse 20.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבֶּ֨ר אִתּ֥וֹ שָׁ֛ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Jacob the name of the place where had spoken with him there God, Bethel.

en.L: And Jacob called the name of the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.
en.B: And the place where God had spoken with him, Jacob called Bethel.
en.R: Jacob named the place where God had talked with him Bethel, which means "house of God."

es.L: Y llamó Jacob el nombre del lugar donde Dios había hablado con él, Betel.
es.B: Y al lugar donde Dios había hablado con él, Jacob lo llamó Betel.
es.R: Jacob llamó Betel al lugar donde Dios había hablado con él. Betel significa «casa de Dios».

fr.L: Et Jacob appela du nom de Béthel le lieu où Dieu avait parlé avec lui.
fr.B: Et ce lieu où Dieu lui avait parlé, Jacob l’appela Béthel.
fr.R: Jacob a appelé Béthel l’endroit où Dieu lui avait parlé. Béthel veut dire « maison de Dieu ».

sw.L: Naye Yakobo akaliita jina la mahali pale Mungu aliposema naye, Betheli.
sw.B: Na mahali pale Mungu aliposema naye, Yakobo akapaita Betheli.
sw.R: Yakobo akapaita Betheli mahali pale Mungu alipozungumza naye, maana yake "nyumba ya Mungu."

decisions.choice: Bethel: the name given again
decisions.reason: Jacob had named the place Bethel, "house of God", on his outward journey (28:19). Naming it again on his return seals what God has done in between.

source.text: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית אֵ֔ל וַֽיְהִי־ע֥וֹד כִּבְרַת־הָאָ֖רֶץ לָב֣וֹא אֶפְרָ֑תָה וַתֵּ֥לֶד רָחֵ֖ל וַתְּקַ֥שׁ בְּלִדְתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they set out from Bethel, and there was yet a stretch of the land to come to Ephrath, and gave birth Rachel, and she had hard labor in her giving birth.

en.L: And they set out from Bethel, and there was still some distance to go to Ephrath, and Rachel went into labor, and she had hard labor in giving birth.
en.B: They moved on from Bethel, and while there was still a stretch of road left before Ephrath, Rachel's time came, and her labor was very hard.
en.R: Then they left Bethel. On the way, before they reached Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth. It was a very hard birth.

es.L: Y partieron de Betel, y aún faltaba un trecho de tierra para llegar a Efrata, y Raquel comenzó a dar a luz, y tuvo un parto difícil.
es.B: Partieron de Betel, y cuando todavía quedaba un trecho de camino para llegar a Efrata, a Raquel le llegó la hora del parto, y fue un parto muy difícil.
es.R: Luego se fueron de Betel. En el camino, antes de llegar a Efrata, Raquel empezó a dar a luz. Fue un parto muy difícil.

fr.L: Et ils partirent de Béthel, et il restait encore une certaine distance pour arriver à Éphrata, et Rachel entra en travail, et son accouchement fut pénible.
fr.B: Ils quittèrent Béthel, et il restait encore un bout de chemin avant Éphrata quand Rachel arriva à son terme ; son accouchement fut très difficile.
fr.R: Ensuite, ils ont quitté Béthel. En chemin, avant d’arriver à Éphrata, Rachel a commencé à accoucher. L’accouchement a été très difficile.

sw.L: Wakasafiri kutoka Betheli, na kulikuwa bado na umbali kidogo kufika Efrathi, Raheli akashikwa na uchungu wa kuzaa, naye akapata shida katika kuzaa kwake.
sw.B: Wakaondoka Betheli, na walipokuwa bado na umbali fulani kabla ya kufika Efrathi, wakati wa Raheli kujifungua ukafika, na uchungu wake ukawa mkali sana.
sw.R: Kisha wakaondoka Betheli. Njiani, kabla hawajafika Efrathi, Raheli akaanza kujifungua. Kuzaa huko kulikuwa kugumu sana.

decisions.choice: a stretch of the land: some distance
decisions.reason: Kivrat ha'arets is an unknown measure of distance, probably a short one (48:7; 2 Kings 5:19).

decisions.choice: Ephrath: the district of Bethlehem
decisions.reason: Ephrath is the older name of the area of Bethlehem (verse 19; Ruth 4:11; Micah 5:2).

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י בְהַקְשֹׁתָ֖הּ בְּלִדְתָּ֑הּ וַתֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֤הּ הַמְיַלֶּ֨דֶת֙ אַל־תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כִּֽי־גַם־זֶ֥ה לָ֖ךְ בֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when she had hard labor in her giving birth, said to her the midwife, do not fear, for also this [one is] for you a son.

en.L: And while she was in hard labor in giving birth, the midwife said to her, "Do not be afraid, for this one too [is] a son for you."
en.B: When her labor was at its worst, the midwife told her, "Do not be afraid; this one is a son for you too."
en.R: While she was struggling to give birth, the woman helping her said, "Do not be afraid. You have another boy!"

es.L: Y sucedió, cuando tenía un parto difícil, que le dijo la partera: «No temas, porque también este [es] un hijo para ti».
es.B: Cuando el parto estaba en su peor momento, la partera le dijo: «No tengas miedo; también este es un hijo para ti».
es.R: Mientras luchaba por dar a luz, la mujer que la ayudaba le dijo: «No tengas miedo. ¡Vas a tener otro niño!».

fr.L: Et il arriva, pendant son accouchement pénible, que la sage-femme lui dit : « Ne crains pas, car celui-ci aussi [est] un fils pour toi. »
fr.B: Au plus fort du travail, la sage-femme lui dit : « N’aie pas peur ; c’est encore un fils pour toi. »
fr.R: Pendant qu’elle avait tant de mal à accoucher, la femme qui l’aidait lui a dit : « N’aie pas peur. Tu as encore un garçon ! »

sw.L: Ikawa, alipokuwa na shida katika kuzaa kwake, mkunga akamwambia, "Usiogope, kwa maana huyu pia [ni] mwana kwako."
sw.B: Uchungu wake ulipokuwa mkali kupita kiasi, mkunga akamwambia, "Usiogope; huyu naye ni mwana kwako."
sw.R: Alipokuwa akihangaika kujifungua, mwanamke aliyekuwa akimsaidia akamwambia, "Usiogope. Umepata mtoto mwingine wa kiume!"

decisions.choice: this one too is a son for you: Rachel's prayer answered
decisions.reason: When Joseph was born, Rachel named him with the prayer "May the LORD add to me another son" (30:24). The midwife tells her the prayer has been answered, even as she dies.

decisions.choice: the woman helping her
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word for a reader who may not know it.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י בְּצֵ֤את נַפְשָׁהּ֙ כִּ֣י מֵ֔תָה וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בֶּן־אוֹנִ֑י וְאָבִ֖יו קָֽרָא־ל֥וֹ בִנְיָמִֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when went out her soul, for she died, and she called his name Ben-oni; and his father called him Benjamin.

en.L: And as her soul was departing, for she was dying, she called his name Ben-oni; but his father called him Benjamin.
en.B: As her life was slipping away, for she was dying, she called him Ben-oni, "son of my sorrow". His father, though, called him Benjamin, "son of the right hand".
en.R: Rachel was dying. With her last breath she named her son Ben-oni, which means "son of my sorrow." But his father named him Benjamin, which means "son of the right hand."

es.L: Y sucedió que, al salírsele el alma, porque se moría, llamó su nombre Ben-oní; pero su padre lo llamó Benjamín.
es.B: Cuando se le escapaba la vida, pues se estaba muriendo, lo llamó Ben-oní, «hijo de mi dolor». Pero su padre lo llamó Benjamín, «hijo de la mano derecha».
es.R: Raquel se estaba muriendo. Con su último aliento llamó a su hijo Ben-oní, que quiere decir «hijo de mi dolor». Pero su padre le puso por nombre Benjamín, que quiere decir «hijo de la mano derecha».

fr.L: Et comme son âme s’en allait, car elle mourait, elle l’appela du nom de Ben-Oni ; mais son père l’appela Benjamin.
fr.B: Alors que sa vie lui échappait, car elle était mourante, elle le nomma Ben-Oni, « fils de ma douleur ». Mais son père l’appela Benjamin, « fils de la main droite ».
fr.R: Rachel était en train de mourir. Dans son dernier souffle, elle a appelé son fils Ben-Oni, ce qui veut dire « fils de ma douleur ». Mais son père l’a appelé Benjamin, ce qui veut dire « fils de la main droite ».

sw.L: Ikawa, roho yake ilipokuwa ikitoka, kwa maana alikuwa akifa, akamwita jina lake Benoni; lakini baba yake akamwita Benyamini.
sw.B: Uhai wake ulipokuwa ukimtoka, kwa kuwa alikuwa akifa, akamwita Benoni, yaani "mwana wa huzuni yangu". Lakini baba yake akamwita Benyamini, yaani "mwana wa mkono wa kuume".
sw.R: Raheli alikuwa akifa. Kwa pumzi yake ya mwisho akampa mwanawe jina Benoni, maana yake "mwana wa huzuni yangu." Lakini baba yake akamwita Benyamini, maana yake "mwana wa mkono wa kuume."

decisions.choice: as her soul was departing: as she breathed her last
decisions.reason: Nefesh is the life or breath; its going out is death.

decisions.choice: Ben-oni: son of my sorrow
decisions.reason: 'Oni can mean trouble or sorrow, which fits Rachel's dying; the same letters can also mean strength or vigor (49:3, of Reuben). The dying mother most likely names her pain.

decisions.choice: Benjamin: son of the right hand
decisions.reason: The right hand stands for strength, favor and good fortune. Since the right is south for one facing east, the name may also mean "son of the south": he is the only son of Jacob born in Canaan, south of Paddan-aram.

source.text: וַתָּ֖מָת רָחֵ֑ל וַתִּקָּבֵר֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אֶפְרָ֔תָה הִ֖וא בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: And died Rachel and was buried on [the] way to Ephrath, that [is] Bethlehem.

en.L: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath, that [is], Bethlehem.
en.B: Rachel died and was laid to rest beside the road to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem.
en.R: So Rachel died. She was buried beside the road to Ephrath, the town now called Bethlehem.

es.L: Y murió Raquel y fue sepultada en el camino a Efrata, esto [es], Belén.
es.B: Raquel murió y fue sepultada junto al camino de Efrata, es decir, Belén.
es.R: Así murió Raquel. La enterraron junto al camino de Efrata, la ciudad que ahora se llama Belén.

fr.L: Et Rachel mourut et fut enterrée sur le chemin d’Éphrata, c’est-à-dire Bethléem.
fr.B: Rachel mourut et fut ensevelie au bord de la route d’Éphrata, c’est-à-dire Bethléem.
fr.R: Rachel est donc morte. On l’a enterrée au bord de la route d’Éphrata, la ville qu’on appelle aujourd’hui Bethléem.

sw.L: Raheli akafa, akazikwa katika njia ya kwenda Efrathi, yaani, Bethlehemu.
sw.B: Raheli akafa, akazikwa kando ya barabara ya kwenda Efrathi, yaani Bethlehemu.
sw.R: Basi Raheli akafa. Akazikwa kando ya njia ya kwenda Efrathi, mji unaoitwa sasa Bethlehemu.

decisions.choice: Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem: Rachel's grave on the way
decisions.reason: Rachel was buried by the road, not in the family tomb at Machpelah. Jeremiah 31:15 pictures Rachel weeping for her children at Ramah, and Matthew 2:18 applies the verse to the children of Bethlehem.

source.text: וַיַּצֵּ֧ב יַעֲקֹ֛ב מַצֵּבָ֖ה עַל־קְבֻרָתָ֑הּ הִ֛וא מַצֶּ֥בֶת קְבֻֽרַת־רָחֵ֖ל עַד־הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And set up Jacob a pillar over her grave; it [is the] pillar of [the] grave of Rachel until this day.

en.L: And Jacob set up a pillar over her grave; it [is] the pillar of Rachel's grave to this day.
en.B: Jacob raised a standing stone over her grave; it is the stone of Rachel's grave, and it stands there to this day.
en.R: Jacob set up a large stone on her grave. It is still there today, showing where Rachel is buried.

es.L: Y Jacob erigió un pilar sobre su sepultura; ese [es] el pilar de la sepultura de Raquel hasta hoy.
es.B: Jacob levantó una estela sobre su tumba; es la estela de la tumba de Raquel, que sigue en pie hasta el día de hoy.
es.R: Jacob puso una piedra grande sobre su tumba. Todavía está allí, y señala dónde está enterrada Raquel.

fr.L: Et Jacob dressa une stèle sur sa tombe ; c’[est] la stèle du tombeau de Rachel jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: Jacob dressa une pierre levée sur sa tombe ; c’est la pierre du tombeau de Rachel, qui est encore là aujourd’hui.
fr.R: Jacob a mis une grande pierre sur sa tombe. Elle est encore là aujourd’hui, et elle montre où Rachel est enterrée.

sw.L: Naye Yakobo akasimamisha nguzo juu ya kaburi lake; hiyo [ndiyo] nguzo ya kaburi la Raheli hata leo.
sw.B: Yakobo akasimamisha jiwe la ukumbusho juu ya kaburi lake; ndilo jiwe la kaburi la Raheli, na lipo hata leo.
sw.R: Yakobo akaweka jiwe kubwa juu ya kaburi lake. Jiwe hilo lipo mpaka leo, likionyesha mahali Raheli alipozikwa.

decisions.choice: to this day: still standing when the account was written
decisions.reason: The phrase tells the first readers that the marker could still be seen. Rachel's tomb is mentioned again as a landmark in 1 Samuel 10:2.

source.text: וַיִּסַּ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּ֣ט אָֽהֳלֹ֔המֵהָ֖לְאָה לְמִגְדַּל־עֵֽדֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And set out Israel and pitched his tent beyond Migdal-eder.

en.L: And Israel set out and pitched his tent beyond Migdal-eder.
en.B: Israel traveled on and pitched his tent on the far side of Migdal-eder.
en.R: Israel moved on and set up his tent past Migdal-eder, which means "tower of the flock."

es.L: Y partió Israel y plantó su tienda más allá de Migdal-éder.
es.B: Israel siguió su camino y plantó su tienda al otro lado de Migdal-éder.
es.R: Israel siguió adelante y puso su tienda más allá de Migdal-éder, que quiere decir «torre del rebaño».

fr.L: Et Israël partit et dressa sa tente au-delà de Migdal-Éder.
fr.B: Israël poursuivit sa route et planta sa tente de l’autre côté de Migdal-Éder.
fr.R: Israël est reparti et il a installé sa tente plus loin que Migdal-Éder, ce qui veut dire « tour du troupeau ».

sw.L: Naye Israeli akasafiri, akapiga hema lake ng'ambo ya Migdal-ederi.
sw.B: Israeli akaendelea na safari, akapiga hema lake upande wa pili wa Migdal-ederi.
sw.R: Israeli akaendelea, akapiga hema lake mbele ya Migdal-ederi, maana yake "mnara wa kundi."

decisions.choice: Israel: the narrator now uses the new name
decisions.reason: From here on Jacob is often called Israel in the story, though not always; both names are used down to the end of the book.

decisions.choice: Migdal-eder: tower of the flock
decisions.reason: A watchtower for shepherds, somewhere between Bethlehem and Hebron. Micah 4:8 uses the name for Jerusalem as a shepherd's tower.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁכֹּ֤ן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֔וא וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ רְאוּבֵ֔ן וַיִּשְׁכַּב֙אֶת־בִּלְהָה֙פִּילֶ֣גֶשׁ אָבִ֔יווַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑לוַיִּֽהְי֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יַעֲקֹ֖ב שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when dwelt Israel in that land, and went Reuben and lay with Bilhah, [the] concubine of his father; and heard Israel. And were the sons of Jacob twelve.

en.L: And while Israel dwelt in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine; and Israel heard [of it]. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.
en.B: During Israel's stay in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and word of it reached Israel. There were twelve sons of Jacob.
en.R: While Israel was living there, his son Reuben had sex with Bilhah, one of his father's wives. Israel found out about it. Jacob had twelve sons.

es.L: Y sucedió, mientras Israel habitaba en aquella tierra, que Rubén fue y se acostó con Bilhá, la concubina de su padre; e Israel [lo] oyó. Y los hijos de Jacob fueron doce.
es.B: Durante la estancia de Israel en aquella tierra, Rubén fue y se acostó con Bilhá, la concubina de su padre, y la noticia llegó a oídos de Israel. Los hijos de Jacob eran doce.
es.R: Mientras Israel vivía allí, su hijo Rubén tuvo relaciones sexuales con Bilhá, una de las esposas de su padre. Israel se enteró. Jacob tenía doce hijos.

fr.L: Et il arriva, pendant qu’Israël habitait dans ce pays, que Ruben alla coucher avec Bilha, la concubine de son père ; et Israël [l’]apprit. Or les fils de Jacob étaient douze.
fr.B: Pendant qu’Israël séjournait dans ce pays, Ruben alla coucher avec Bilha, la concubine de son père, et Israël en fut informé. Les fils de Jacob étaient au nombre de douze.
fr.R: Pendant qu’Israël habitait là, son fils Ruben a couché avec Bilha, l’une des femmes de son père. Israël l’a appris. Jacob avait douze fils.

sw.L: Ikawa, Israeli alipokuwa akikaa katika nchi ile, Reubeni akaenda akalala na Bilha suria wa baba yake; naye Israeli akasikia [habari]. Basi wana wa Yakobo walikuwa kumi na wawili.
sw.B: Israeli alipokuwa akiishi katika nchi ile, Reubeni akaenda akalala na Bilha, suria wa baba yake, na habari hizo zikamfikia Israeli. Wana wa Yakobo walikuwa kumi na wawili.
sw.R: Israeli alipokuwa akiishi huko, mwanawe Reubeni alifanya ngono na Bilha, mmoja wa wake za baba yake. Israeli akapata habari. Yakobo alikuwa na wana kumi na wawili.

decisions.choice: lay with Bilhah his father's concubine: a claim to his father's place
decisions.reason: To take a ruler's or father's concubine was a bid for his authority (2 Samuel 16:21-22; 1 Kings 2:22). Bilhah was Rachel's slave woman and mother of Dan and Naphtali (30:3-8). For this Reuben lost the firstborn's rights (49:3-4; 1 Chronicles 5:1).

decisions.choice: and Israel heard of it: the Hebrew stops here
alternatives: and Israel heard, and it was evil in his sight
decisions.reason: The Masoretic text marks a paragraph break in the middle of this verse, after "Israel heard", as if the silence were deliberate. The Greek translation adds "and it seemed evil to him". The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: concubine: a wife of lower rank
decisions.reason: A pilegesh was a secondary wife, often a former slave, without the full rights of a principal wife. Bilhah is called both Jacob's wife (30:4) and his concubine.

decisions.choice: one of his father's wives
decisions.reason: Readable avoids the unfamiliar word "concubine"; Bilhah is also called Jacob's wife in 30:4.

source.text: בְּנֵ֣י לֵאָ֔ה בְּכ֥וֹר יַעֲקֹ֖ב רְאוּבֵ֑ן וְשִׁמְעוֹן֙ וְלֵוִ֣י וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְיִשָּׂשכָ֖ר וּזְבוּלֻֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Leah: [the] firstborn of Jacob, Reuben, and Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Zebulun.

en.L: The sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun.
en.B: Leah's sons were Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, then Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun.
en.R: Leah's sons were Reuben, who was Jacob's oldest son, and Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun.

es.L: Los hijos de Lea: Rubén, el primogénito de Jacob, y Simeón, Leví, Judá, Isacar y Zabulón.
es.B: Los hijos de Lea fueron Rubén, el primogénito de Jacob, y luego Simeón, Leví, Judá, Isacar y Zabulón.
es.R: Los hijos de Lea eran Rubén, que era el hijo mayor de Jacob, y Simeón, Leví, Judá, Isacar y Zabulón.

fr.L: Les fils de Léa : Ruben, le premier-né de Jacob, et Siméon, Lévi, Juda, Issacar et Zabulon.
fr.B: Les fils de Léa étaient Ruben, le premier-né de Jacob, puis Siméon, Lévi, Juda, Issacar et Zabulon.
fr.R: Les fils de Léa étaient Ruben, le fils aîné de Jacob, et Siméon, Lévi, Juda, Issacar et Zabulon.

sw.L: Wana wa Lea: Reubeni, mzaliwa wa kwanza wa Yakobo, na Simeoni, Lawi, Yuda, Isakari na Zabuloni.
sw.B: Wana wa Lea walikuwa Reubeni, mzaliwa wa kwanza wa Yakobo, kisha Simeoni, Lawi, Yuda, Isakari na Zabuloni.
sw.R: Wana wa Lea walikuwa Reubeni, aliyekuwa mwana mkubwa wa Yakobo, na Simeoni, Lawi, Yuda, Isakari na Zabuloni.

decisions.choice: the sons of Leah: the twelve listed by their mothers
decisions.reason: The list groups the sons by mother: Leah's six, Rachel's two, and two each for the slave wives Bilhah and Zilpah. Reuben is still named firstborn, right after the wrong of verse 22.

source.text: בְּנֵ֣י רָחֵ֔ל יוֹסֵ֖ף וּבִנְיָמִֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

en.L: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
en.B: Rachel's sons were Joseph and Benjamin.
en.R: Rachel's sons were Joseph and Benjamin.

es.L: Los hijos de Raquel: José y Benjamín.
es.B: Los hijos de Raquel fueron José y Benjamín.
es.R: Los hijos de Raquel eran José y Benjamín.

fr.L: Les fils de Rachel : Joseph et Benjamin.
fr.B: Les fils de Rachel étaient Joseph et Benjamin.
fr.R: Les fils de Rachel étaient Joseph et Benjamin.

sw.L: Wana wa Raheli: Yusufu na Benyamini.
sw.B: Wana wa Raheli walikuwa Yusufu na Benyamini.
sw.R: Wana wa Raheli walikuwa Yusufu na Benyamini.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֤י בִלְהָה֙ שִׁפְחַ֣ת רָחֵ֔ל דָּ֖ן וְנַפְתָּלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Bilhah, [the] slave woman of Rachel: Dan and Naphtali.

en.L: And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's slave woman: Dan and Naphtali.
en.B: The sons of Bilhah, Rachel's servant, were Dan and Naphtali.
en.R: The sons of Bilhah, Rachel's servant, were Dan and Naphtali.

es.L: Y los hijos de Bilhá, la esclava de Raquel: Dan y Neftalí.
es.B: Los hijos de Bilhá, la sierva de Raquel, fueron Dan y Neftalí.
es.R: Los hijos de Bilhá, la sierva de Raquel, eran Dan y Neftalí.

fr.L: Et les fils de Bilha, l’esclave de Rachel : Dan et Nephtali.
fr.B: Les fils de Bilha, la servante de Rachel, étaient Dan et Nephtali.
fr.R: Les fils de Bilha, la servante de Rachel, étaient Dan et Nephtali.

sw.L: Na wana wa Bilha, mtumwa wa kike wa Raheli: Dani na Naftali.
sw.B: Wana wa Bilha, mtumishi wa Raheli, walikuwa Dani na Naftali.
sw.R: Wana wa Bilha, mtumishi wa Raheli, walikuwa Dani na Naftali.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וּבְנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה גָּ֣ד וְאָשֵׁ֑ר אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלַּד־ל֖וֹ בְּפַדַּ֥ן אֲרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Zilpah, [the] slave woman of Leah: Gad and Asher. These [are the] sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-aram.

en.L: And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's slave woman: Gad and Asher. These [are] the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-aram.
en.B: The sons of Zilpah, Leah's servant, were Gad and Asher. These were Jacob's sons, born to him in Paddan-aram.
en.R: The sons of Zilpah, Leah's servant, were Gad and Asher. These were Jacob's sons. They were born in Paddan-aram.

es.L: Y los hijos de Zilpá, la esclava de Lea: Gad y Aser. Estos [son] los hijos de Jacob que le nacieron en Padán Aram.
es.B: Los hijos de Zilpá, la sierva de Lea, fueron Gad y Aser. Estos fueron los hijos de Jacob, que le nacieron en Padán Aram.
es.R: Los hijos de Zilpá, la sierva de Lea, eran Gad y Aser. Estos eran los hijos de Jacob. Nacieron en Padán Aram.

fr.L: Et les fils de Zilpa, l’esclave de Léa : Gad et Aser. Ce [sont] là les fils de Jacob qui lui naquirent à Paddân-Aram.
fr.B: Les fils de Zilpa, la servante de Léa, étaient Gad et Aser. Tels furent les fils de Jacob, qui lui naquirent à Paddân-Aram.
fr.R: Les fils de Zilpa, la servante de Léa, étaient Gad et Aser. C’étaient les fils de Jacob. Ils sont nés à Paddân-Aram.

sw.L: Na wana wa Zilpa, mtumwa wa kike wa Lea: Gadi na Asheri. Hao [ndio] wana wa Yakobo waliozaliwa kwake huko Padan-aramu.
sw.B: Wana wa Zilpa, mtumishi wa Lea, walikuwa Gadi na Asheri. Hao ndio wana wa Yakobo, waliozaliwa kwake huko Padan-aramu.
sw.R: Wana wa Zilpa, mtumishi wa Lea, walikuwa Gadi na Asheri. Hao ndio wana wa Yakobo. Walizaliwa huko Padan-aramu.

decisions.choice: born to him in Paddan-aram: a summary of the whole list
decisions.reason: The closing line sums up the twelve as a group. Benjamin, the one exception, has just been born in Canaan (verses 16-18); the summary speaks of the family as a whole.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־יִצְחָ֣ק אָבִ֔יו מַמְרֵ֖א קִרְיַ֣ת הָֽאַרְבַּ֑ע הִ֣וא חֶבְר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־גָּֽר־שָׁ֥ם אַבְרָהָ֖ם וְיִצְחָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Jacob to Isaac his father [at] Mamre, Kiriath-arba, that [is] Hebron, where had sojourned Abraham and Isaac.

en.L: And Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mamre, at Kiriath-arba, that [is], Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had sojourned.
en.B: Jacob finally reached his father Isaac at Mamre, by Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where first Abraham and then Isaac had lived as foreigners.
en.R: At last Jacob reached his father Isaac's home at Mamre, near the town of Kiriath-arba, now called Hebron. Abraham and Isaac had both lived there as foreigners.

es.L: Y llegó Jacob a Isaac su padre, a Mamre, a Quiriat-arbá, esto [es], Hebrón, donde habían residido como extranjeros Abraham e Isaac.
es.B: Por fin Jacob llegó adonde estaba su padre Isaac, en Mamre, junto a Quiriat-arbá (es decir, Hebrón), donde primero Abraham y luego Isaac habían vivido como extranjeros.
es.R: Por fin Jacob llegó a la casa de su padre Isaac en Mamre, cerca de la ciudad de Quiriat-arbá, que ahora se llama Hebrón. Abraham e Isaac habían vivido allí como extranjeros.

fr.L: Et Jacob vint vers Isaac son père, à Mamré, à Kiryath-Arba, c’est-à-dire Hébron, où Abraham et Isaac avaient séjourné en étrangers.
fr.B: Jacob arriva enfin chez son père Isaac, à Mamré, près de Kiryath-Arba (c’est-à-dire Hébron), là où Abraham, puis Isaac, avaient vécu en étrangers.
fr.R: Enfin, Jacob est arrivé chez son père Isaac, à Mamré, près de la ville de Kiryath-Arba, qu’on appelle aujourd’hui Hébron. Abraham et Isaac avaient tous les deux vécu là comme étrangers.

sw.L: Naye Yakobo akafika kwa Isaka baba yake huko Mamre, huko Kiriath-arba, yaani, Hebroni, ambako Abrahamu na Isaka walikaa kama wageni.
sw.B: Hatimaye Yakobo akamfikia baba yake Isaka huko Mamre, karibu na Kiriath-arba (yaani Hebroni), ambako kwanza Abrahamu na kisha Isaka waliishi kama wageni.
sw.R: Mwishowe Yakobo akafika nyumbani kwa baba yake Isaka huko Mamre, karibu na mji wa Kiriath-arba, unaoitwa sasa Hebroni. Abrahamu na Isaka wote wawili waliishi huko kama wageni.

decisions.choice: Mamre, Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron: Abraham's old home
decisions.reason: Mamre was where Abraham settled and built an altar (13:18), and where he bought the burial cave (23:2, 19). Kiriath-arba ("town of Arba") was the older name of Hebron (Joshua 14:15).

decisions.choice: sojourned: lived as resident foreigners
decisions.reason: Abraham and Isaac lived in the land as outsiders who did not own it, except for the grave they had bought (23:4).

source.text: וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ יְמֵ֣י יִצְחָ֑ק מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֖ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And were the days of Isaac one hundred years and eighty years.

en.L: And the days of Isaac were 180 years.
en.B: Isaac lived to the age of 180.
en.R: Isaac lived to be 180 years old.

es.L: Y los días de Isaac fueron ciento ochenta años.
es.B: Isaac vivió hasta los ciento ochenta años.
es.R: Isaac vivió ciento ochenta años.

fr.L: Et les jours d’Isaac furent de cent quatre-vingts ans.
fr.B: Isaac vécut jusqu’à l’âge de cent quatre-vingts ans.
fr.R: Isaac a vécu jusqu’à cent quatre-vingts ans.

sw.L: Na siku za Isaka zilikuwa miaka mia moja na themanini.
sw.B: Isaka akaishi hadi umri wa miaka mia moja na themanini.
sw.R: Isaka aliishi miaka mia moja na themanini.

source.text: וַיִּגְוַ֨ע יִצְחָ֤ק וַיָּ֨מָת֙ וַיֵּאָ֣סֶף אֶל־עַמָּ֔יו זָקֵ֖ן וּשְׂבַ֣ע יָמִ֑ים וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ עֵשָׂ֥ו וְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בָּנָֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And breathed his last Isaac and died and was gathered to his people, old and satisfied of days; and buried him Esau and Jacob his sons.

en.L: And Isaac breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days; and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.
en.B: Isaac's breath failed, and he died and was gathered to his people, an old man who had his fill of years. His sons Esau and Jacob laid him in the grave.
en.R: Then Isaac died. He was very old and had lived a long, full life. He joined his family members who had died before him. His sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

es.L: Y expiró Isaac y murió, y fue reunido con su pueblo, viejo y lleno de días; y lo sepultaron Esaú y Jacob sus hijos.
es.B: Isaac exhaló su último aliento y murió, y fue reunido con su pueblo, anciano y saciado de años. Sus hijos Esaú y Jacob lo sepultaron.
es.R: Entonces Isaac murió. Era muy anciano y había tenido una vida larga y plena. Se reunió con los de su familia que habían muerto antes que él. Sus hijos Esaú y Jacob lo enterraron.

fr.L: Et Isaac expira et mourut, et il fut réuni à son peuple, vieux et rassasié de jours ; et Ésaü et Jacob, ses fils, l’enterrèrent.
fr.B: Isaac rendit le dernier souffle ; il mourut et fut réuni à son peuple, âgé et comblé d’années. Ses fils Ésaü et Jacob le mirent au tombeau.
fr.R: Puis Isaac est mort. Il était très âgé et avait eu une vie longue et bien remplie. Il a rejoint les membres de sa famille morts avant lui. Ses fils Ésaü et Jacob l’ont enterré.

sw.L: Naye Isaka akakata roho, akafa, akakusanywa pamoja na watu wake, mzee aliyeshiba siku; nao Esau na Yakobo wanawe wakamzika.
sw.B: Pumzi ya Isaka ikakoma, akafa, akakusanywa kwa watu wake, mzee aliyeshiba miaka. Wanawe Esau na Yakobo wakamzika kaburini.
sw.R: Kisha Isaka akafa. Alikuwa mzee sana, na alikuwa ameishi maisha marefu na mazuri. Akajiunga na watu wa jamaa yake waliokufa kabla yake. Wanawe Esau na Yakobo wakamzika.

decisions.choice: was gathered to his people: joined his ancestors in death
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Abraham (25:8) and Ishmael (25:17). It speaks of death as joining those who went before, not only of burial.

decisions.choice: old and full of days: satisfied with a long life
decisions.reason: Said also of Abraham (25:8). Isaac's death is told here, though he may have lived on into the years of the Joseph story; Genesis closes one family's account before beginning the next.

decisions.choice: Esau and Jacob his sons buried him: the brothers together at the grave
decisions.reason: As Isaac and Ishmael buried Abraham (25:9), so the two rival brothers bury their father together, in the cave of Machpelah (49:31). Esau is named first, as the older son.
